card.law_is_about: Motions to repeal a COVID-19 vaccination requirement for workers in health and care facilities and investigate adverse effects.
card.they_want: Repeal the facility-specific vaccination mandate immediately.
card.they_claim: From nearly equal crude Danish household infection rates, even boosters did not reduce onward infection risk at all.
card.the_problem: The crude rates do not identify a causal absence of protection, while the same study reports an adjusted protective association. But the author expressly adopts crude absolute rates, so a proven factual or source-description error is not established.

claim_quote.original: und damit das Ansteckungsrisiko auch enger Kontaktpersonen somit gar nicht.
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: and therefore did not reduce the infection risk even for close contacts at all.

locator.paragraph: first, final clause; subject in preceding clause is two-dose and booster vaccination

request_quote.translation_en: Translation: repeal of the facility-specific vaccination mandate

counter_quote.original: booster vaccination did offer some protection against household transmission

correction: The copied supplement gives crude secondary attack rates by the primary case’s vaccine status. The main adjusted model reports a pooled primary-case booster odds ratio of0.80(95%CI0.69–0.92) versus fully vaccinated and describes some protection. These are different estimands. The author accurately reproduces the descriptive table, expressly prefers absolute SAR differences on page20, and then draws its own inference. Neither crude equality nor the adjusted observational association alone establishes the actual causal risk claim.
effect: Unresolved: if an affirmative misattribution or factual no-protection error were established, it would weaken a central empirical argument for repeal. The present evidence instead establishes differing analyses and an under-supported inference, which is insufficient to classify a proved error under this project’s rules.
limits: No proved factual/source-description error is alleged on present evidence. The author does not expressly attribute a no-protection conclusion to the study authors. An omitted adjusted observational association does not by itself make the author’s preferred crude-rate inference factually false. The adjusted estimate pools Delta and Omicron and acknowledges residual confounding, misclassification and uncertain duration; it is not an Omicron-only causal estimate. No conclusion about mandate necessity, proportionality, current protection or care-facility efficacy follows.
context_and_alternatives: All34 author pages were read. Page20 expressly adopts differences in absolute household SARs as its effectiveness measure. Page23 correctly introduces the descriptive rates before its own inferential step, and pages22–24 argue against reliable protection. This supports a methodological-inference reading rather than a false quotation or claimed adjusted study conclusion. The adjusted model supplies an affirmative reason to question the categorical inference but does not resolve the causal claim. The small30/31% running-text discrepancy is not promoted separately.
materiality_explanation: Potential major materiality if a categorical factual error or affirmative source misattribution were independently established: absence of protection is central to the repeal argument. That error has not been established, so this is an unresolved lead rather than a major finding.
direction_explanation: True only for the tested hypothesis: a categorical no-protection claim supports repeal. This records argumentative direction, not a finding that the claim is false or any intent.
